disclaimer: Informational, not legal advice. Verify with the legislation, the Energy Networks Association and your own Distribution Network Operator before relying on any value here.

notification.deadline_source: stated on the operator's own page
notification.deadline_quote: Customer/Installer must notify SSEN of the connection within 28 days from the date of commissioning
notification.deadline_context: Stated in the operator's own MPAN process document REF-PS-066 Rev 2.0 (2025) rather than on the G98 documents page. The same document states there is no requirement to contact SSEN prior to installation.
notification.route_note: The operator's document addresses "Customer/Installer". That identifies who completes the form; it does not state that a customer may notify without an installer. Recorded as unknown rather than read as permission.
notification.fee_note: not verified - no operator page consulted states a fee for a single-premises G98 notification, and we do not infer that it is free
notification.legal_basis: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002

national_rule.quote: the Installer is required to ensure that the DNO is made aware of the Micro-generator installation before the time of commissioning or no later than 28 days (inclusive of the day of commissioning) after commissioning
national_rule.source_document: ENA Engineering Recommendation G98, section 1.1 (restated at 8.3.1)
national_rule.legal_basis: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002 Regulation 22(2)(c), and the Certificate of Exemption granted by the Health and Safety Executive in August 2008
national_rule.duty_holder_quote: Your installer must notify the DNO within 28 days of commissioning the generating unit, and provide them with information on the installation. This is a legal requirement.
national_rule.duty_holder_source: ENA Distributed Generation Connection Guide: G98 for Single Premises
national_rule.form: G98 Form B, the Installation Document at Appendix 3 of EREC G98
national_rule.applies_to_diy_householder_note: EREC G98 places the duty on the installer, and still does. No primary source consulted stated what a householder who installs a plug-in device without an installer must do until the Energy Networks Association published a registration portal at https://myplugin.solar/ , read 2026-09-02, whose FAQ states that registering the device there sends the notification to the DNO, and that registration is a legal requirement. That claim is the portal's own; its Terms of Use cite 'the regulations relating to these devices' without naming them. This field stays null because EREC G98 itself is unchanged: it names the installer, not the householder.
national_rule.not_referenced_by_si_2026_848_note: The full text of SI 2026/848 was read on 2026-08-01. It amends product safety requirements and does not mention EREC G98, DNO notification, or any connection procedure. The notification framework is separate from the legalisation.

limits.legal_product_cap_applies_to: whether a device is a plug-in microgenerator under SI 2026/848
limits.note: Two different caps apply and they are often confused. 800 W is the product cap set by SI 2026/848 for something to count as a plug-in microgenerator. 3.68 kW per phase is the connection-process cap for Engineering Recommendation G98. They serve different purposes.

legislation_summary.note: Regulation 3 of SI 2026/848 extends to England and Wales and Scotland. All licence areas in this file are within that extent.
